module.title: Describing Physical Appearance & Style
module.objective: Describe physical appearance, height, hair style, facial features, and personal style using appropriate descriptive adjectives.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: What Do They Look Like?

content.summary: Welcome to your Reading Mission! In this lesson, you will read a fun passage about people and their physical appearance. You will learn how to understand descriptions of height, hair color, hair style, face shape, and accessories like glasses. By the end of this mission, you will feel confident reading and understanding how people describe what someone looks like in English. Let's get started!

linguisticTarget.grammar: Using 'be' (am/is/are) + adjective for general body characteristics (tall, short, slim) and 'have got / has got' + noun phrase for specific features someone possesses (curly hair, brown eyes, a beard). Using 'wear/wears' for accessories.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words for height (tall, short, medium height), hair (curly, straight, wavy, blonde, brown, black, long, short), face (round, oval), and accessories (glasses, moustache, beard).
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skimming the passage first to understand the main idea (Who is being described?), then scanning for key details (What does each person look like?). Look for adjectives near 'is/are' and noun phrases after 'has got / have got' to find appearance details quickly.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short A1 passage about people's physical appearance.
Identify key details including height, hair color, hair style, face shape, and accessories.
Recognize the correct use of 'be' for general characteristics and 'have got / has got' for owned features.
Distinguish between 'be', 'have got', and 'wear' when reading descriptions of people.
Build confidence reading simple descriptive texts about what people look like.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your friend asks you: 'What does your best friend look like?' Which answer correctly describes physical appearance?
options: She is tall and she has got long brown hair.
She likes pizza and she plays guitar.
She is happy and she has got a new phone.
contextWarmup.explanation: Option 1 is correct because it describes physical appearance — height ('tall') and hair ('long brown hair'). Option 2 talks about hobbies and food, not appearance. Option 3 describes mood and possessions, not what someone looks like.

rules: Use 'be' (am/is/are) + adjective to describe general body characteristics: 'He is tall.' 'She is slim.' 'They are short.'
Use 'have got' (I/you/we/they) or 'has got' (he/she/it) + noun phrase to describe features someone possesses: 'I have got brown eyes.' 'She has got curly hair.' 'He has got a beard.'
Use 'wear' (I/you/we/they) or 'wears' (he/she/it) for accessories and clothing items: 'She wears glasses.' 'He wears a hat.'
When reading, look for the verb to know what type of description follows: after 'is/are' expect an adjective; after 'has got/have got' expect a noun phrase.
Adjective order matters in descriptions: size + shape + color + noun. For example: 'long straight black hair' (not 'black long straight hair').

commonTrap.trapTitle: Common Beginner Pitfall: Mixing Up 'Be' and 'Have Got'
commonTrap.explanation: Many beginners confuse 'be' and 'have got' when reading descriptions. Remember: 'be' (is/are) comes before adjectives that describe general characteristics like height or body type. 'Have got / has got' comes before noun phrases that describe features someone possesses, like hair, eyes, or a beard. When you see 'She is...' expect an adjective (tall, slim). When you see 'She has got...' expect a noun phrase (brown eyes, curly hair).
commonTrap.wrong: She is long black hair. He has got tall.
commonTrap.correct: She has got long black hair. He is tall.

content.context: A student named Mia is writing a short blog post for her English class. She is describing the people in her favourite family photo. Read her description carefully and notice how she talks about what each person looks like.
content.text:
This is my favourite family photo! There are four people in the picture: my dad, my mum, my brother Leo, and me.

My dad is tall and he has got short straight black hair. He has got a beard and a moustache. He wears glasses too. He has got a round face and brown eyes.

My mum is medium height and slim. She has got long wavy brown hair and an oval face. She has got big green eyes. She is very pretty!

My brother Leo is quite short because he is only twelve years old. He has got curly blonde hair and a round face. He looks like my dad, but he does not have a beard, of course!

And me? I am tall and slim, like my mum. I have got long straight black hair and brown eyes, like my dad. I wear glasses for reading. We are a happy family!

'Has got' + noun phrase for facial hair feature

gistQuestion.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Mia describes what her family members look like in a photo.
Mia talks about her family's favourite hobbies.
Mia explains where her family lives.
gistQuestion.explanation: The passage is about Mia describing the physical appearance of each family member in a photo. She talks about their height, hair, face shape, and accessories. She does not talk about hobbies or where they live.

detailQuestions.prompt: What does Mia's dad look like?
options: He is tall, has got short straight black hair, a beard, a moustache, and he wears glasses.
He is short, has got long curly brown hair, and he does not wear glasses.
He is medium height, has got wavy blonde hair, and he has got green eyes.
detailQuestions.explanation: The passage says Mia's dad 'is tall', 'has got short straight black hair', 'has got a beard and a moustache', and 'wears glasses'. He also has a round face and brown eyes.

detailQuestions.prompt: What face shape does Mia's mum have?
options: She has got an oval face.
She has got a round face.
She has got a square face.
detailQuestions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Mia's mum 'has got long wavy brown hair and an oval face.' The round face belongs to Mia's dad and brother Leo.

options: Because he is only twelve years old.
Because he has got curly hair.
detailQuestions.explanation: Mia explains that Leo 'is quite short because he is only twelve years old.' His height is related to his age, not to wearing glasses or having curly hair.

options: She looks like both her mum (tall and slim) and her dad (black hair and brown eyes).
She looks exactly like her brother Leo.
She looks like her mum only.
detailQuestions.explanation: Mia says she is 'tall and slim, like my mum' and she has 'long straight black hair and brown eyes, like my dad.' So she has features from both parents.

questions.question: According to the passage, what colour are Mia's mum's eyes?
questions.explanation: The passage says Mia's mum 'has got big green eyes.' Brown eyes belong to Mia's dad and Mia herself.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct structure to describe someone's hair?
options: She has got long wavy brown hair.
She is long wavy brown hair.
She has long wavy brown hair got.
questions.answer: She has got long wavy brown hair.
questions.explanation: Hair is a feature someone possesses, so we use 'has got' + noun phrase. 'She is long wavy brown hair' incorrectly uses 'be'. The third option has incorrect word order.

questions.question: In the passage, who has got a round face? (Choose the best answer.)
options: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
questions.answer: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
questions.explanation: The passage says Mia's dad 'has got a round face' and Leo 'has got curly blonde hair and a round face.' Mia's mum has an oval face. Mia does not mention her own face shape.

questions.question: Which word describes hair that has gentle curves — not straight and not curly?
questions.explanation: 'Wavy' describes hair with gentle curves, between straight and curly. 'Blonde' is a hair colour, and 'slim' describes body type, not hair.

questions.question: Read this sentence: 'He _____ glasses.' Which word correctly completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: We use 'wears' (from the verb 'wear') for accessories like glasses, hats, and uniforms. 'Has got' is for features someone possesses (hair, eyes). 'Is' is for general characteristics (tall, slim).

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Leo's hair look like?
options: He has got curly blonde hair.
He has got straight black hair.
He has got long wavy brown hair.
questions.answer: He has got curly blonde hair.
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Leo 'has got curly blonde hair.' Straight black hair belongs to Mia's dad, and long wavy brown hair belongs to Mia's mum.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'She is slim' and 'She has got brown eyes'?
options: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
'Is' and 'has got' mean the same thing.
'Has got' describes a general characteristic; 'is' describes a feature someone possesses.
questions.answer: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
questions.explanation: We use 'be' (is/are) + adjective for general body characteristics like height and body type. We use 'have got / has got' + noun phrase for specific features someone possesses, like eyes, hair, or a beard.

questions.question: Mia says she wears glasses. What does she use them for?
questions.explanation: Mia says 'I wear glasses for reading.' The passage does not mention swimming or cooking.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: What Does She Look Like?

content.summary: In this listening mission, you will hear two friends talking at a café. One friend describes another person's physical appearance — her height, hair colour, hair style, eye colour, and whether she wears glasses. Listen carefully for adjectives that describe the body and face. Pay attention to the phrase 'What does she look like?' because this is the key question we use to ask about someone's appearance. Also notice how speakers use 'She has got...' to describe permanent features and 'She is wearing...' to describe clothes right now.
learningObjectives: Understand and identify descriptions of physical appearance such as height, hair, and eyes in spoken English.
Recognise the question 'What does she look like?' and understand its meaning in context.
Distinguish between 'She has got...' for permanent features and 'She is wearing...' for current clothing.
Identify key adjectives for appearance: tall, slim, long, straight, black, brown, blue.

keyPhrases.note: This is the main question to ask about someone's physical appearance. Do not confuse it with 'What does she like?' which asks about preferences.

keyPhrases.phrase: She has got long straight black hair.
keyPhrases.meaning: Dia punya rambut hitam lurus panjang.
keyPhrases.note: Use 'has got' to describe permanent physical features. Notice the adjective order: length (long) + shape (straight) + colour (black) + noun (hair).
Use 'wears' with simple present tense for things a person usually wears every day, like glasses.
'Quite' means 'fairly' or 'rather'. It softens the adjective. 'Tall' describes height, and 'slim' describes a thin body shape.
Use 'has got + colour + eyes' to describe eye colour. Common eye colours: brown, blue, green, black.

keyPhrases.phrase: She's wearing a blue jacket today.
keyPhrases.meaning: Dia sedang memakai jaket biru hari ini.
keyPhrases.note: Use 'is wearing' (present continuous) to describe what someone is wearing right now, at this moment.

connectedSpeech.note: In fast speech, 'What does' blends together. The 't' in 'what' becomes a quick flap sound, and 'does' reduces to 'duhz' or even 'uhz'. Listen for the 'look like' at the end to recognise this question.

connectedSpeech.slow: She has got long straight black hair.
connectedSpeech.fast: She's got long straight black hair.
connectedSpeech.slowIpa: /ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ streɪt blæk heər/
connectedSpeech.note: 'She has got' contracts to 'She's got' in natural speech. The 'r' at the end of 'hair' is often very soft or silent in British English.
In casual speech, 'Yes' often becomes 'Yeah'. The word 'she' is slightly shorter and less stressed.

connectedSpeech.slow: Is that her near the door?
connectedSpeech.note: 'Is that' links together so the 'z' sound connects directly to 'that'. The 'h' in 'her' is often dropped in fast speech, making it sound like 'er'.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Describe How People Look

content.summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to write sentences and short paragraphs to describe a person's physical appearance and style. You will use three important structures: 'be + adjective' to describe general characteristics, 'have got / has got' to talk about body features a person has, and 'wear / wears' to talk about accessories and clothing. By the end, you can write a short description of anyone you know!

blueprintItems.title: Describe Features with 'Have Got / Has Got'
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + have got / has got + (adjective) + noun.
blueprintItems.example: He has got short brown hair and blue eyes.

blueprintItems.title: Describe Accessories and Clothing with 'Wear / Wears'
blueprintItems.example: She wears round glasses and a red scarf.

blueprintItems.title: Combine All Three Structures in a Short Paragraph
blueprintItems.formula: Sentence 1 (be + adjective) + Sentence 2 (have got/has got) + Sentence 3 (wear/wears).
blueprintItems.example: My brother is tall. He has got curly black hair and brown eyes. He wears a blue cap every day.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always start a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop.
mechanicsRules.why: Every English sentence must begin with a capital letter and finish with a full stop (period). This shows where a sentence starts and ends.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'has got' for he, she, and it. Use 'have got' for I, you, we, and they.
mechanicsRules.why: Third-person singular subjects (he, she, it) always take 'has got', not 'have got'. This is a subject-verb agreement rule.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'wears' for he, she, and it. Use 'wear' for I, you, we, and they.
mechanicsRules.why: In the simple present tense, third-person singular subjects need an '-s' at the end of the verb. So 'wear' becomes 'wears' for he, she, and it.

mechanicsRules.rule: Put adjectives before the noun they describe.
mechanicsRules.badExample: She has got hair long and brown.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: She has got long brown hair.
mechanicsRules.why: In English, adjectives come before the noun. When you use two adjectives, the order is usually: size + colour + noun (for example, 'long brown hair').

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: Describe Your Best Friend
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write a short paragraph (3 to 5 sentences) to describe your best friend's appearance. Use 'is/are + adjective' for general looks, 'has got / have got' for hair, eyes, and face, and 'wears' for any accessories or clothing they usually have. Remember to start each sentence with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
guidedLabChallenges.example: My best friend is tall and slim. She has got long straight black hair and dark brown eyes. She has got an oval face. She wears small silver earrings. She is very pretty.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Describe a Family Member
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Choose one person in your family (mother, father, brother, sister, grandmother, etc.). Write 4 to 6 sentences about their physical appearance and style. Describe their height, build, hair, eyes, face shape, and any accessories they wear. Use all three structures you have learned: 'be + adjective', 'has got / have got + noun', and 'wears + accessory'.
guidedLabChallenges.example: My grandfather is old and short. He has got white hair and grey eyes. He has got a round face and a big nose. He wears thick glasses. He also wears a brown hat when he goes outside. He is very kind.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Look at this information about a girl named Lily: Height: short, Hair: long, curly, red, Eyes: green, Face: round, Accessories: glasses, a yellow scarf. Write 4 sentences to describe Lily. Use 'is', 'has got', and 'wears'.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The answer must include at least 4 complete sentences. It must correctly use 'is + adjective' for height or general look, 'has got + adjective + noun' for hair, eyes, and face, and 'wears + noun' for accessories. Each sentence must start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Adjectives must come before nouns.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: Lily is short. She has got long curly red hair and green eyes. She has got a round face. She wears glasses and a yellow scarf.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Describe yourself in 3 to 5 sentences. Write about your height, your hair (colour and style), your eyes, and anything you usually wear (glasses, a watch, a hat, etc.). Use 'I am', 'I have got', and 'I wear'.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The answer must include at least 3 complete sentences. It must use 'I am + adjective' for general appearance, 'I have got + adjective + noun' for physical features, and 'I wear + noun' for accessories or clothing. Correct capitalization and punctuation are required. Adjective order should be correct (size before colour before noun).
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: I am tall and thin. I have got short black hair and brown eyes. I have got an oval face. I wear a silver watch every day.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Your teacher asks you to describe two classmates. Write a short paragraph (5 to 7 sentences) about two people in your class. Describe their height, hair, eyes, and style. Use 'is/are', 'has got / have got', and 'wears / wear'.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The answer must include at least 5 complete sentences describing two different people. It must correctly use 'is + adjective' and 'are + adjective' for general appearance, 'has got' for singular subjects and 'have got' for plural or first/second person, and 'wears' for singular and 'wear' for plural subjects. Proper capitalization of names and sentence beginnings is required. Each sentence must end with a full stop.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: My classmate Tom is tall and strong. He has got short brown hair and blue eyes. He wears a black watch. My classmate Sari is short and slim. She has got long straight black hair and dark brown eyes. She has got a round face. She wears small red glasses.

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Describing Physical Appearance & Style

content.summary: In this speaking lab, you will learn how to describe people's physical appearance clearly and confidently. You will practise saying words for height, hair colour, hair style, face shape, and accessories like glasses. Good pronunciation and natural intonation will help people understand your descriptions easily. We will focus on stressing the right syllables in appearance words, using rising and falling intonation in questions and statements, and linking words smoothly when you speak.
content.audioGuidance: When describing someone, speak slowly and clearly. Stress the important describing words (adjectives) like TALL, SHORT, CURLY, STRAIGHT. Use falling intonation for statements like 'He is tall.' and rising intonation for yes/no questions like 'Does she wear glasses?' Pause slightly between description phrases to sound natural, for example: 'She has got... long curly hair... and brown eyes.'

pillars.name: Adjective Stress & Clarity
pillars.target: Pronounce appearance adjectives with correct syllable stress
pillars.explanation: When you describe someone, the adjectives carry the most important information. Words like 'curly' (CUR-ly), 'glasses' (GLASS-es), and 'moustache' (mous-TACHE) need correct stress so your listener understands you. Always stress the capitalised syllable and say the other syllables more softly.

pillars.name: Intonation in Descriptions
pillars.target: Use falling intonation for statements and rising intonation for yes/no questions
pillars.explanation: When you make a statement like 'He has got short hair', your voice should go DOWN at the end. When you ask a yes/no question like 'Does she wear glasses?', your voice should go UP at the end. This helps your listener know if you are telling or asking.

pillars.name: Linking & Fluency with 'have got'
pillars.target: Connect words smoothly when using 'have got' and 'has got' structures
pillars.explanation: In natural speech, 'have got' often sounds like 'have-got' with the words linked together. Practise saying 'She has got long hair' as a smooth phrase: 'She-has-got-long-hair'. Do not pause between every single word. This makes your speech sound more fluent and natural.

pillars.name: List Intonation for Multiple Features
pillars.target: Use rising intonation on list items and falling intonation on the last item
pillars.explanation: When you describe several features, your voice should rise slightly on each item in the list and fall on the last one. For example: 'He is TALL ↗, he has got SHORT HAIR ↗, and he wears GLASSES ↘.' This pattern tells your listener when the list is finished.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: When 'curly' stands alone, the stress is on the first syllable: CUR-ly. But in the compound adjective 'curly-haired', the stress often shifts to emphasise the second part, linking the hair type to the noun.
In 'glasses', the stress is on GLASS. When we add 'sun' to make 'sunglasses', the stress stays on GLASS but the rhythm changes because there is an extra syllable at the beginning.
Both 'appear' and 'appearance' keep the stress on the second syllable PEAR. Notice that 'appearance' adds the suffix '-ance' but the stress does not move. This is a helpful pattern to remember.

In 'shoulder', the stress is on SHOUL. In the compound 'shoulder-length', both SHOUL and LENGTH receive stress because it is a compound adjective. This double stress pattern is common in compound descriptions.

drills.targetText: She has got long straight hair.
drills.focus: Clear pronunciation of 'straight' and linking 'has got'
drills.hint: Make sure 'straight' rhymes with 'late'. Link 'has got' smoothly so it sounds like one word: 'hazgot'.

drills.targetText: He is tall and slim with brown eyes.
drills.phonetic: /hiː ɪz tɔːl ænd slɪm wɪð braʊn aɪz/
drills.hint: For 'with', put your tongue gently between your teeth for the 'th' sound. Do not say 'wid' or 'wif'.

drills.targetText: My mother has got short curly hair and a round face.
drills.phonetic: /maɪ ˈmʌðər hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt ˈkɜːli heər ænd ə raʊnd feɪs/
drills.hint: Stress the describing words: SHORT, CUR-ly, ROUND. These are the most important words for your listener to hear.
This is a yes/no question, so your voice should go UP at the end on 'glasses?' Like going up a staircase.

drills.targetText: He has got a beard and a moustache.
drills.phonetic: /hiː hæz ɡɒt ə bɪəd ænd ə məˈstɑːʃ/
drills.hint: Say 'moustache' with the stress on the second syllable: mous-TACHE. The 'ou' sounds like the 'u' in 'must'.

drills.targetText: What does your sister look like?
drills.focus: Falling intonation for Wh-question and linking 'look like'
drills.hint: This is a Wh-question, so your voice goes DOWN at the end. Link 'look like' smoothly: 'looklike'.

roleplay.context: You are meeting Mr. Khoirul, your English tutor, for a speaking practice session. He wants to practise describing people's physical appearance. He will ask you to describe yourself, your best friend, and a family member. Use 'be' for height and body type, and 'have got' for hair, eyes, and face features. Answer his questions with full sentences.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! Today we are going to practise describing people. Let's start with you. Can you describe your appearance? For example, are you tall or short?
turns.translation: Halo! Hari ini kita akan berlatih mendeskripsikan orang. Mari mulai dari kamu. Bisakah kamu mendeskripsikan penampilanmu? Misalnya, apakah kamu tinggi atau pendek?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I am quite tall. I have got short black hair and brown eyes.
turns.translation: Saya cukup tinggi. Saya punya rambut hitam pendek dan mata cokelat.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Great! Do you wear glasses or have any other distinctive features?
turns.translation: Bagus! Apakah kamu memakai kacamata atau punya ciri khas lainnya?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, I wear glasses. I have got a round face.
turns.translation: Ya, saya memakai kacamata. Saya punya wajah bulat.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Excellent! Now, can you describe your best friend? What does he or she look like?
turns.translation: Luar biasa! Sekarang, bisakah kamu mendeskripsikan sahabatmu? Seperti apa penampilannya?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: My best friend is short and slim. She has got long curly hair and she does not wear glasses.
turns.translation: Sahabat saya pendek dan langsing. Dia punya rambut panjang keriting dan dia tidak memakai kacamata.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Very good! What about your father? Can you describe him using 'be' and 'have got'?
turns.translation: Bagus sekali! Bagaimana dengan ayahmu? Bisakah kamu mendeskripsikannya menggunakan 'be' dan 'have got'?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: My father is tall. He has got short grey hair and a moustache. He wears glasses too.
turns.translation: Ayah saya tinggi. Dia punya rambut pendek beruban dan kumis. Dia juga memakai kacamata.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about meeting a new classmate for the first time. Describe what this person looks like. Use 'be' for height and body type, and 'have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Follow the three story points below.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Imagine you are at school and you meet a new classmate. Tell me about this person. What does he or she look like? Describe the person's height, hair, eyes, and any special features like glasses.
storyPoints: Describe the new classmate's height and body type using 'be' (for example: tall, short, slim, medium height).
Describe the classmate's hair colour, hair length, and eye colour using 'have got'.
Mention one or two special features such as glasses, a beard, freckles, or a round face.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My new classmate is tall and slim. He has got short brown hair and blue eyes. He wears glasses and he has got a long face.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ njuː ˈklɑːsmeɪt ɪz tɔːl ænd slɪm. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt braʊn heər ænd bluː aɪz. hiː weəz ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ə lɒŋ feɪs/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember to use 'is' for height and body shape, and 'has got' for hair, eyes, and face features. Speak slowly and clearly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This storytelling task practises using 'be' and 'have got' together to give a complete physical description. Good descriptions include height, body type, hair, eyes, and special features.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about looking at a family photo. Describe two people in the photo. Use 'be' and 'have got' to describe their physical appearance.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: You are looking at a family photo. Choose two people in the photo and describe what they look like. Talk about their height, hair, eyes, and any special features.
storyPoints: Introduce the first person in the photo and describe their height, hair, and eyes.
Introduce the second person and describe how they look different from the first person.
Mention any accessories or special features for one or both people, such as glasses, a hat, or a moustache.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: In the photo, my grandmother is short. She has got long white hair and green eyes. My uncle is very tall. He has got short black hair and a big moustache. He wears sunglasses.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪn ðə ˈfəʊtəʊ maɪ ˈɡrænmʌðər ɪz ʃɔːt. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ waɪt heər ænd ɡriːn aɪz. maɪ ˈʌŋkl ɪz ˈveri tɔːl. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt blæk heər ænd ə bɪɡ məˈstɑːʃ. hiː weəz ˈsʌnɡlɑːsɪz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe two different people so you can practise contrasting descriptions. Use words like 'but' or 'and' to connect your sentences.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing two people in contrast helps you practise a wider range of appearance vocabulary. It also trains you to organise your ideas clearly when speaking.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are calling your friend to describe a person you saw at the park. Your friend wants to know what this person looks like. Describe the person's height, hair, and face.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Your friend answers the phone and says: 'Hi! You said you saw someone interesting at the park. What does this person look like?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are on a phone call with your friend. You saw an interesting-looking person at the park today and you want to describe them. Your friend will ask you follow-up questions about the person's appearance.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student calling your friend to describe a stranger you saw at the park. Be descriptive and use 'be' and 'have got'.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The person is very tall and thin. He has got long red hair and a beard. He has got a long face and big green eyes.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈpɜːsn ɪz ˈveri tɔːl ænd θɪn. hiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ red heər ænd ə bɪəd. hiː hæz ɡɒt ə lɒŋ feɪs ænd bɪɡ ɡriːn aɪz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with the person's height and body type, then move to hair and face details. Use 'has got' for features.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In this roleplay, you practise describing a person naturally in a phone conversation. This is a real-life situation where you need to paint a picture with words.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a lost-and-found office. A police officer asks you to describe your lost friend so they can help find them. Describe your friend's appearance clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The police officer says: 'Hello. Can you describe your friend? What does your friend look like? Is your friend tall or short? What colour is their hair?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at a lost-and-found office in a shopping mall. You have lost your friend and a police officer needs a clear description to help find them. You must describe your friend's height, hair, eyes, and what makes them easy to recognise.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a worried student at a lost-and-found office. You need to describe your friend's physical appearance to a police officer so they can find your friend.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My friend is medium height and slim. She has got long straight black hair and dark brown eyes. She wears red glasses and she has got a round face.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ frend ɪz ˈmiːdiəm haɪt ænd slɪm. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ streɪt blæk heər ænd dɑːk braʊn aɪz. ʃiː weəz red ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd ʃiː hæz ɡɒt ə raʊnd feɪs/
practicumQuestions.hint: Be very specific. The police officer needs details! Mention height, hair style, hair colour, eye colour, and special features like glasses.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing someone to help find them is a very practical real-life skill. You need to be clear and specific so the listener can identify the person.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are video-calling your pen pal for the first time. Your pen pal asks you to describe yourself. Tell them what you look like.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your pen pal says on the video call: 'Wow, it is so nice to finally see you! But my camera is not working well. Can you describe yourself for me? What do you look like?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are on a video call with your pen pal from another country. The video quality is very bad, so your pen pal asks you to describe your own physical appearance using words. This is the first time you are talking to each other.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student meeting your international pen pal on a video call for the first time. Describe your own appearance clearly and confidently.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I am quite short. I have got medium-length brown hair and dark eyes. I have got an oval face and I do not wear glasses.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ æm kwaɪt ʃɔːt. aɪ hæv ɡɒt ˈmiːdiəm leŋθ braʊn heər ænd dɑːk aɪz. aɪ hæv ɡɒt ən ˈəʊvl feɪs ænd aɪ duː nɒt weər ˈɡlɑːsɪz/
practicumQuestions.hint: You are describing yourself, so use 'I am' for height and 'I have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Be honest and detailed!
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing yourself is one of the most common speaking tasks at A1 level. Using 'I am' and 'I have got' correctly shows good grammar control.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a party and you see your teacher's new hairstyle. Your teacher asks you what you think. Describe what you notice about their new look.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your teacher, Mrs. Sari, says: 'Hello! I have got a new hairstyle today. Can you describe how I look now? What is different about my hair?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at a school party and your teacher, Mrs. Sari, has a new hairstyle. She used to have long straight hair, but now her hair is different. She asks you to describe her new appearance. Be polite and descriptive.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a polite student at a school party. You need to describe your teacher's new hairstyle and overall appearance. Use kind and descriptive words.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Mrs. Sari, you look very nice! You have got short curly hair now. It is brown with blonde highlights. Your hair looks really beautiful.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈmɪsɪz ˈsɑːri juː lʊk ˈveri naɪs. juː hæv ɡɒt ʃɔːt ˈkɜːli heər naʊ. ɪt ɪz braʊn wɪð blɒnd ˈhaɪlaɪts. jɔːr heər lʊks ˈrɪəli ˈbjuːtɪfl/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with a compliment, then describe what you see. Use 'have got' to describe the new hair. Be polite!
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises describing changes in appearance and giving polite compliments. It combines appearance vocabulary with social language skills.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Focus on using the correct vocabulary words for physical appearance.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence clearly: 'My brother is medium height. He has got wavy blonde hair, blue eyes, and freckles.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My brother is medium height. He has got wavy blonde hair, blue eyes, and freckles.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈbrʌðər ɪz ˈmiːdiəm haɪt. hiː hæz ɡɒt ˈweɪvi blɒnd heər bluː aɪz ænd ˈfreklz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Focus on the appearance words: 'medium height', 'wavy', 'blonde', and 'freckles'. Make sure each word is clear and easy to understand.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill tests your knowledge of key appearance vocabulary. Words like 'wavy', 'blonde', and 'freckles' are essential for describing people at A1 level.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay attention to the correct use of 'be' for height and 'have got' for features.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence. Be careful with the grammar: 'She is short and slim. She has got long straight hair and she has not got a fringe.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: She is short and slim. She has got long straight hair and she has not got a fringe.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz ʃɔːt ænd slɪm. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ streɪt heər ænd ʃiː hæz nɒt ɡɒt ə frɪndʒ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'is' for body type (short, slim) and 'has got' for hair features. For the negative, say 'has not got'. Do not mix up 'is' and 'has got'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This grammar drill practises the two key structures for describing appearance: 'be + adjective' for height and body type, and 'have got + noun' for physical features. The negative form 'has not got' is also important.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay special attention to the syllable stress on the underlined words. Stress the capitalised syllables.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence and stress the correct syllables: 'She has got BEAU-ti-ful SHOUL-der-length hair and a mous-TACHE is not COM-mon for women.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: She has got beautiful shoulder-length hair and a moustache is not common for women.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ʃiː hæz ɡɒt ˈbjuːtɪfl ˈʃəʊldə leŋθ heər ænd ə məˈstɑːʃ ɪz nɒt ˈkɒmən fɔːr ˈwɪmɪn/
practicumQuestions.hint: Stress the first syllable in BEAU-ti-ful, SHOUL-der, and COM-mon. Stress the second syllable in mous-TACHE. Say WI-men, not 'wo-men'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Syllable stress changes the rhythm of English. Words like 'beautiful' (BEAU-ti-ful) and 'moustache' (mous-TACHE) have different stress positions. Practising these patterns helps you sound more natural.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following two sentences out loud. Use FALLING intonation for the statement and RISING intonation for the yes/no question.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say these two sentences with the correct intonation. First, the statement with falling intonation: 'He has got short grey hair.' Then, the question with rising intonation: 'Does he wear glasses?'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: He has got short grey hair. Does he wear glasses?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt ɡreɪ heər ↘ dʌz hiː weər ˈɡlɑːsɪz ↗/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the statement 'He has got short grey hair', let your voice go DOWN at the end like going down a slide. For the question 'Does he wear glasses?', let your voice go UP at the end like climbing stairs.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In English, statements use falling intonation to show you are finished speaking. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to show you are asking and expecting an answer. This intonation pattern is very important for clear communication.

reading.question: According to the passage, what colour are Mia's mum's eyes?
reading.explanation: The passage says Mia's mum 'has got big green eyes.' Brown eyes belong to Mia's dad and Mia herself.

reading.question: Which sentence uses the correct structure to describe someone's hair?
options: She has got long wavy brown hair.
She is long wavy brown hair.
She has long wavy brown hair got.
reading.answer: She has got long wavy brown hair.
reading.explanation: Hair is a feature someone possesses, so we use 'has got' + noun phrase. 'She is long wavy brown hair' incorrectly uses 'be'. The third option has incorrect word order.

reading.question: In the passage, who has got a round face? (Choose the best answer.)
options: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
reading.answer: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
reading.explanation: The passage says Mia's dad 'has got a round face' and Leo 'has got curly blonde hair and a round face.' Mia's mum has an oval face. Mia does not mention her own face shape.

reading.question: Which word describes hair that has gentle curves — not straight and not curly?
reading.explanation: 'Wavy' describes hair with gentle curves, between straight and curly. 'Blonde' is a hair colour, and 'slim' describes body type, not hair.

reading.question: Read this sentence: 'He _____ glasses.' Which word correctly completes the sentence?
reading.explanation: We use 'wears' (from the verb 'wear') for accessories like glasses, hats, and uniforms. 'Has got' is for features someone possesses (hair, eyes). 'Is' is for general characteristics (tall, slim).

reading.question: According to the passage, what does Leo's hair look like?
options: He has got curly blonde hair.
He has got straight black hair.
He has got long wavy brown hair.
reading.answer: He has got curly blonde hair.
reading.explanation: The passage clearly states that Leo 'has got curly blonde hair.' Straight black hair belongs to Mia's dad, and long wavy brown hair belongs to Mia's mum.

reading.question: What is the difference between 'She is slim' and 'She has got brown eyes'?
options: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
'Is' and 'has got' mean the same thing.
'Has got' describes a general characteristic; 'is' describes a feature someone possesses.
reading.answer: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
reading.explanation: We use 'be' (is/are) + adjective for general body characteristics like height and body type. We use 'have got / has got' + noun phrase for specific features someone possesses, like eyes, hair, or a beard.

reading.question: Mia says she wears glasses. What does she use them for?
reading.explanation: Mia says 'I wear glasses for reading.' The passage does not mention swimming or cooking.

reading.question: What is Jamie's nationality?
reading.explanation: Jamie is from Spain, so his nationality is Spanish.

reading.question: Which sentence is the correct negative form of 'She likes coffee'?
reading.explanation: For third person singular (she/he/it), we use 'doesn't + base verb'.

reading.question: Where do they usually eat dinner on weekdays?
reading.explanation: Daily routines typically describe having dinner at home with family.

reading.question: What time does the train to London depart?
reading.explanation: Standard timetable questions provide specific morning departure times.

reading.question: Choose the correct past form: 'Yesterday, we _____ a new car.'
reading.explanation: 'Buy' is an irregular verb whose past simple form is 'bought'.

reading.question: What does Maria do every Saturday morning?
reading.explanation: A routine action in the simple present tense describing Saturday morning.

reading.question: Which question is grammatically correct?
reading.explanation: Standard question order: Question Word + Auxiliary (do) + Subject (you) + Verb (live).

writing.criteria: The answer must include at least 4 complete sentences. It must correctly use 'is + adjective' for height or general look, 'has got + adjective + noun' for hair, eyes, and face, and 'wears + noun' for accessories. Each sentence must start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Adjectives must come before nouns.
writing.sampleGoodAnswer: Lily is short. She has got long curly red hair and green eyes. She has got a round face. She wears glasses and a yellow scarf.

writing.prompt: Describe yourself in 3 to 5 sentences. Write about your height, your hair (colour and style), your eyes, and anything you usually wear (glasses, a watch, a hat, etc.). Use 'I am', 'I have got', and 'I wear'.

It must use 'I am + adjective' for general appearance, 'I have got + adjective + noun' for physical features, and 'I wear + noun' for accessories or clothing. Correct capitalization and punctuation are required. Adjective order should be correct (size before colour before noun).

writing.prompt: Your teacher asks you to describe two classmates. Write a short paragraph (5 to 7 sentences) about two people in your class. Describe their height, hair, eyes, and style. Use 'is/are', 'has got / have got', and 'wears / wear'.

speaking.instruction: Tell a short story about meeting a new classmate for the first time. Describe what this person looks like. Use 'be' for height and body type, and 'have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Follow the three story points below.
speaking.audioPrompt: Imagine you are at school and you meet a new classmate. Tell me about this person. What does he or she look like? Describe the person's height, hair, eyes, and any special features like glasses.
storyPoints: Describe the new classmate's height and body type using 'be' (for example: tall, short, slim, medium height).
Describe the classmate's hair colour, hair length, and eye colour using 'have got'.
Mention one or two special features such as glasses, a beard, freckles, or a round face.
speaking.targetSentence: My new classmate is tall and slim. He has got short brown hair and blue eyes. He wears glasses and he has got a long face.
speaking.phonetic: /maɪ njuː ˈklɑːsmeɪt ɪz tɔːl ænd slɪm. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt braʊn heər ænd bluː aɪz. hiː weəz ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ə lɒŋ feɪs/
speaking.hint: Remember to use 'is' for height and body shape, and 'has got' for hair, eyes, and face features. Speak slowly and clearly.
speaking.explanation: This storytelling task practises using 'be' and 'have got' together to give a complete physical description. Good descriptions include height, body type, hair, eyes, and special features.

speaking.instruction: Tell a short story about looking at a family photo. Describe two people in the photo. Use 'be' and 'have got' to describe their physical appearance.
speaking.audioPrompt: You are looking at a family photo. Choose two people in the photo and describe what they look like. Talk about their height, hair, eyes, and any special features.
storyPoints: Introduce the first person in the photo and describe their height, hair, and eyes.
Introduce the second person and describe how they look different from the first person.
Mention any accessories or special features for one or both people, such as glasses, a hat, or a moustache.
speaking.targetSentence: In the photo, my grandmother is short. She has got long white hair and green eyes. My uncle is very tall. He has got short black hair and a big moustache. He wears sunglasses.
speaking.phonetic: /ɪn ðə ˈfəʊtəʊ maɪ ˈɡrænmʌðər ɪz ʃɔːt. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ waɪt heər ænd ɡriːn aɪz. maɪ ˈʌŋkl ɪz ˈveri tɔːl. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt blæk heər ænd ə bɪɡ məˈstɑːʃ. hiː weəz ˈsʌnɡlɑːsɪz/
speaking.hint: Describe two different people so you can practise contrasting descriptions. Use words like 'but' or 'and' to connect your sentences.
speaking.explanation: Describing two people in contrast helps you practise a wider range of appearance vocabulary. It also trains you to organise your ideas clearly when speaking.

speaking.instruction: You are calling your friend to describe a person you saw at the park. Your friend wants to know what this person looks like. Describe the person's height, hair, and face.

speaking.targetSentence: The person is very tall and thin. He has got long red hair and a beard. He has got a long face and big green eyes.

speaking.explanation: In this roleplay, you practise describing a person naturally in a phone conversation. This is a real-life situation where you need to paint a picture with words.

speaking.instruction: You are at a lost-and-found office. A police officer asks you to describe your lost friend so they can help find them. Describe your friend's appearance clearly.

speaking.characterRole: You are a worried student at a lost-and-found office. You need to describe your friend's physical appearance to a police officer so they can find your friend.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct structure to describe someone's hair?
options: She has got long wavy brown hair.
She is long wavy brown hair.
She has long wavy brown hair got.
questions.answer: She has got long wavy brown hair.
questions.explanation: Hair is a feature someone possesses, so we use 'has got' + noun phrase. 'She is long wavy brown hair' incorrectly uses 'be'. The third option has incorrect word order.

questions.question: In the passage, who has got a round face? (Choose the best answer.)
options: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
questions.answer: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
questions.explanation: The passage says Mia's dad 'has got a round face' and Leo 'has got curly blonde hair and a round face.' Mia's mum has an oval face. Mia does not mention her own face shape.

questions.question: Which word describes hair that has gentle curves — not straight and not curly?
questions.explanation: 'Wavy' describes hair with gentle curves, between straight and curly. 'Blonde' is a hair colour, and 'slim' describes body type, not hair.

questions.question: Read this sentence: 'He _____ glasses.' Which word correctly completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: We use 'wears' (from the verb 'wear') for accessories like glasses, hats, and uniforms. 'Has got' is for features someone possesses (hair, eyes). 'Is' is for general characteristics (tall, slim).

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Leo's hair look like?
options: He has got curly blonde hair.
He has got straight black hair.
He has got long wavy brown hair.
questions.answer: He has got curly blonde hair.
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Leo 'has got curly blonde hair.' Straight black hair belongs to Mia's dad, and long wavy brown hair belongs to Mia's mum.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'She is slim' and 'She has got brown eyes'?
options: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
'Is' and 'has got' mean the same thing.
'Has got' describes a general characteristic; 'is' describes a feature someone possesses.
questions.answer: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
questions.explanation: We use 'be' (is/are) + adjective for general body characteristics like height and body type. We use 'have got / has got' + noun phrase for specific features someone possesses, like eyes, hair, or a beard.

questions.question: Mia says she wears glasses. What does she use them for?

questions.question: What is Jamie's nationality?
questions.explanation: Jamie is from Spain, so his nationality is Spanish.

questions.question: Which sentence is the correct negative form of 'She likes coffee'?
questions.explanation: For third person singular (she/he/it), we use 'doesn't + base verb'.

questions.question: Where do they usually eat dinner on weekdays?
questions.explanation: Daily routines typically describe having dinner at home with family.

questions.question: Which question is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: Standard question order: Question Word + Auxiliary (do) + Subject (you) + Verb (live).

questions.instruction: Tell a short story about meeting a new classmate for the first time. Describe what this person looks like. Use 'be' for height and body type, and 'have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Follow the three story points below.
questions.audioPrompt: Imagine you are at school and you meet a new classmate. Tell me about this person. What does he or she look like? Describe the person's height, hair, eyes, and any special features like glasses.
storyPoints: Describe the new classmate's height and body type using 'be' (for example: tall, short, slim, medium height).
Describe the classmate's hair colour, hair length, and eye colour using 'have got'.
Mention one or two special features such as glasses, a beard, freckles, or a round face.
questions.targetSentence: My new classmate is tall and slim. He has got short brown hair and blue eyes. He wears glasses and he has got a long face.
questions.phonetic: /maɪ njuː ˈklɑːsmeɪt ɪz tɔːl ænd slɪm. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt braʊn heər ænd bluː aɪz. hiː weəz ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ə lɒŋ feɪs/
questions.hint: Remember to use 'is' for height and body shape, and 'has got' for hair, eyes, and face features. Speak slowly and clearly.
questions.explanation: This storytelling task practises using 'be' and 'have got' together to give a complete physical description. Good descriptions include height, body type, hair, eyes, and special features.

questions.instruction: Tell a short story about looking at a family photo. Describe two people in the photo. Use 'be' and 'have got' to describe their physical appearance.
questions.audioPrompt: You are looking at a family photo. Choose two people in the photo and describe what they look like. Talk about their height, hair, eyes, and any special features.
storyPoints: Introduce the first person in the photo and describe their height, hair, and eyes.
Introduce the second person and describe how they look different from the first person.
Mention any accessories or special features for one or both people, such as glasses, a hat, or a moustache.
questions.targetSentence: In the photo, my grandmother is short. She has got long white hair and green eyes. My uncle is very tall. He has got short black hair and a big moustache. He wears sunglasses.
questions.phonetic: /ɪn ðə ˈfəʊtəʊ maɪ ˈɡrænmʌðər ɪz ʃɔːt. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ waɪt heər ænd ɡriːn aɪz. maɪ ˈʌŋkl ɪz ˈveri tɔːl. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt blæk heər ænd ə bɪɡ məˈstɑːʃ. hiː weəz ˈsʌnɡlɑːsɪz/
questions.hint: Describe two different people so you can practise contrasting descriptions. Use words like 'but' or 'and' to connect your sentences.
questions.explanation: Describing two people in contrast helps you practise a wider range of appearance vocabulary. It also trains you to organise your ideas clearly when speaking.

questions.instruction: You are calling your friend to describe a person you saw at the park. Your friend wants to know what this person looks like. Describe the person's height, hair, and face.
questions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Your friend answers the phone and says: 'Hi! You said you saw someone interesting at the park. What does this person look like?'
questions.scenarioContext: You are on a phone call with your friend. You saw an interesting-looking person at the park today and you want to describe them. Your friend will ask you follow-up questions about the person's appearance.
questions.characterRole: You are a student calling your friend to describe a stranger you saw at the park. Be descriptive and use 'be' and 'have got'.
questions.targetSentence: The person is very tall and thin. He has got long red hair and a beard. He has got a long face and big green eyes.

questions.hint: Start with the person's height and body type, then move to hair and face details. Use 'has got' for features.
questions.explanation: In this roleplay, you practise describing a person naturally in a phone conversation. This is a real-life situation where you need to paint a picture with words.

questions.instruction: You are at a lost-and-found office. A police officer asks you to describe your lost friend so they can help find them. Describe your friend's appearance clearly.
questions.audioPrompt: The police officer says: 'Hello. Can you describe your friend? What does your friend look like? Is your friend tall or short? What colour is their hair?'
questions.scenarioContext: You are at a lost-and-found office in a shopping mall. You have lost your friend and a police officer needs a clear description to help find them. You must describe your friend's height, hair, eyes, and what makes them easy to recognise.
questions.characterRole: You are a worried student at a lost-and-found office. You need to describe your friend's physical appearance to a police officer so they can find your friend.
questions.targetSentence: My friend is medium height and slim. She has got long straight black hair and dark brown eyes. She wears red glasses and she has got a round face.
questions.phonetic: /maɪ frend ɪz ˈmiːdiəm haɪt ænd slɪm. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ streɪt blæk heər ænd dɑːk braʊn aɪz. ʃiː weəz red ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd ʃiː hæz ɡɒt ə raʊnd feɪs/
questions.hint: Be very specific. The police officer needs details! Mention height, hair style, hair colour, eye colour, and special features like glasses.
questions.explanation: Describing someone to help find them is a very practical real-life skill. You need to be clear and specific so the listener can identify the person.

questions.characterRole: You are a student meeting your international pen pal on a video call for the first time. Describe your own appearance clearly and confidently.
questions.targetSentence: I am quite short. I have got medium-length brown hair and dark eyes. I have got an oval face and I do not wear glasses.

questions.hint: You are describing yourself, so use 'I am' for height and 'I have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Be honest and detailed!
questions.explanation: Describing yourself is one of the most common speaking tasks at A1 level. Using 'I am' and 'I have got' correctly shows good grammar control.

questions.instruction: You are at a party and you see your teacher's new hairstyle. Your teacher asks you what you think. Describe what you notice about their new look.

questions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay attention to the correct use of 'be' for height and 'have got' for features.

questions.hint: Use 'is' for body type (short, slim) and 'has got' for hair features. For the negative, say 'has not got'. Do not mix up 'is' and 'has got'.
questions.explanation: This grammar drill practises the two key structures for describing appearance: 'be + adjective' for height and body type, and 'have got + noun' for physical features. The negative form 'has not got' is also important.

questions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay special attention to the syllable stress on the underlined words. Stress the capitalised syllables.
questions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence and stress the correct syllables: 'She has got BEAU-ti-ful SHOUL-der-length hair and a mous-TACHE is not COM-mon for women.'
questions.targetSentence: She has got beautiful shoulder-length hair and a moustache is not common for women.

questions.hint: Stress the first syllable in BEAU-ti-ful, SHOUL-der, and COM-mon. Stress the second syllable in mous-TACHE. Say WI-men, not 'wo-men'.
questions.explanation: Syllable stress changes the rhythm of English. Words like 'beautiful' (BEAU-ti-ful) and 'moustache' (mous-TACHE) have different stress positions. Practising these patterns helps you sound more natural.

questions.instruction: Say the following two sentences out loud. Use FALLING intonation for the statement and RISING intonation for the yes/no question.

questions.hint: For the statement 'He has got short grey hair', let your voice go DOWN at the end like going down a slide. For the question 'Does he wear glasses?', let your voice go UP at the end like climbing stairs.
questions.explanation: In English, statements use falling intonation to show you are finished speaking. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to show you are asking and expecting an answer. This intonation pattern is very important for clear communication.

practicumQuestions.question: According to the passage, what colour are Mia's mum's eyes?
practicumQuestions.explanation: The passage says Mia's mum 'has got big green eyes.' Brown eyes belong to Mia's dad and Mia herself.

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence uses the correct structure to describe someone's hair?
options: She has got long wavy brown hair.
She is long wavy brown hair.
She has long wavy brown hair got.
practicumQuestions.answer: She has got long wavy brown hair.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Hair is a feature someone possesses, so we use 'has got' + noun phrase. 'She is long wavy brown hair' incorrectly uses 'be'. The third option has incorrect word order.

practicumQuestions.question: In the passage, who has got a round face? (Choose the best answer.)
options: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
practicumQuestions.answer: Mia's dad and her brother Leo
practicumQuestions.explanation: The passage says Mia's dad 'has got a round face' and Leo 'has got curly blonde hair and a round face.' Mia's mum has an oval face. Mia does not mention her own face shape.

practicumQuestions.question: Which word describes hair that has gentle curves — not straight and not curly?
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Wavy' describes hair with gentle curves, between straight and curly. 'Blonde' is a hair colour, and 'slim' describes body type, not hair.

practicumQuestions.question: Read this sentence: 'He _____ glasses.' Which word correctly completes the sentence?
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use 'wears' (from the verb 'wear') for accessories like glasses, hats, and uniforms. 'Has got' is for features someone possesses (hair, eyes). 'Is' is for general characteristics (tall, slim).

practicumQuestions.question: According to the passage, what does Leo's hair look like?
options: He has got curly blonde hair.
He has got straight black hair.
He has got long wavy brown hair.
practicumQuestions.answer: He has got curly blonde hair.
practicumQuestions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Leo 'has got curly blonde hair.' Straight black hair belongs to Mia's dad, and long wavy brown hair belongs to Mia's mum.

practicumQuestions.question: What is the difference between 'She is slim' and 'She has got brown eyes'?
options: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
'Is' and 'has got' mean the same thing.
'Has got' describes a general characteristic; 'is' describes a feature someone possesses.
practicumQuestions.answer: 'Is' describes a general characteristic; 'has got' describes a feature someone possesses.
practicumQuestions.explanation: We use 'be' (is/are) + adjective for general body characteristics like height and body type. We use 'have got / has got' + noun phrase for specific features someone possesses, like eyes, hair, or a beard.

practicumQuestions.question: Mia says she wears glasses. What does she use them for?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Mia says 'I wear glasses for reading.' The passage does not mention swimming or cooking.

practicumQuestions.question: What is Jamie's nationality?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Jamie is from Spain, so his nationality is Spanish.

practicumQuestions.question: Which sentence is the correct negative form of 'She likes coffee'?
practicumQuestions.explanation: For third person singular (she/he/it), we use 'doesn't + base verb'.

practicumQuestions.question: Where do they usually eat dinner on weekdays?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Daily routines typically describe having dinner at home with family.

practicumQuestions.question: What time does the train to London depart?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Standard timetable questions provide specific morning departure times.

practicumQuestions.question: Choose the correct past form: 'Yesterday, we _____ a new car.'
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Buy' is an irregular verb whose past simple form is 'bought'.

practicumQuestions.question: What does Maria do every Saturday morning?
practicumQuestions.explanation: A routine action in the simple present tense describing Saturday morning.

practicumQuestions.question: Which question is grammatically correct?
practicumQuestions.explanation: Standard question order: Question Word + Auxiliary (do) + Subject (you) + Verb (live).

practicumQuestions.prompt: Look at this information about a girl named Lily: Height: short, Hair: long, curly, red, Eyes: green, Face: round, Accessories: glasses, a yellow scarf. Write 4 sentences to describe Lily. Use 'is', 'has got', and 'wears'.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The answer must include at least 4 complete sentences. It must correctly use 'is + adjective' for height or general look, 'has got + adjective + noun' for hair, eyes, and face, and 'wears + noun' for accessories. Each sentence must start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Adjectives must come before nouns.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: Lily is short. She has got long curly red hair and green eyes. She has got a round face. She wears glasses and a yellow scarf.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Describe yourself in 3 to 5 sentences. Write about your height, your hair (colour and style), your eyes, and anything you usually wear (glasses, a watch, a hat, etc.). Use 'I am', 'I have got', and 'I wear'.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The answer must include at least 3 complete sentences. It must use 'I am + adjective' for general appearance, 'I have got + adjective + noun' for physical features, and 'I wear + noun' for accessories or clothing. Correct capitalization and punctuation are required. Adjective order should be correct (size before colour before noun).
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: I am tall and thin. I have got short black hair and brown eyes. I have got an oval face. I wear a silver watch every day.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Your teacher asks you to describe two classmates. Write a short paragraph (5 to 7 sentences) about two people in your class. Describe their height, hair, eyes, and style. Use 'is/are', 'has got / have got', and 'wears / wear'.
practicumQuestions.criteria: The answer must include at least 5 complete sentences describing two different people. It must correctly use 'is + adjective' and 'are + adjective' for general appearance, 'has got' for singular subjects and 'have got' for plural or first/second person, and 'wears' for singular and 'wear' for plural subjects. Proper capitalization of names and sentence beginnings is required. Each sentence must end with a full stop.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: My classmate Tom is tall and strong. He has got short brown hair and blue eyes. He wears a black watch. My classmate Sari is short and slim. She has got long straight black hair and dark brown eyes. She has got a round face. She wears small red glasses.

practicumQuestions.hint: 'This' menjadi 'These', 'child' menjadi 'children', 'is' menjadi 'are'.
targetAnswers: These children are playing in the park.
These children are playing in the park
practicumQuestions.explanation: Bentuk jamak dari 'this child is' adalah 'these children are'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about meeting a new classmate for the first time. Describe what this person looks like. Use 'be' for height and body type, and 'have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Follow the three story points below.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Imagine you are at school and you meet a new classmate. Tell me about this person. What does he or she look like? Describe the person's height, hair, eyes, and any special features like glasses.
storyPoints: Describe the new classmate's height and body type using 'be' (for example: tall, short, slim, medium height).
Describe the classmate's hair colour, hair length, and eye colour using 'have got'.
Mention one or two special features such as glasses, a beard, freckles, or a round face.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My new classmate is tall and slim. He has got short brown hair and blue eyes. He wears glasses and he has got a long face.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ njuː ˈklɑːsmeɪt ɪz tɔːl ænd slɪm. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt braʊn heər ænd bluː aɪz. hiː weəz ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ə lɒŋ feɪs/
practicumQuestions.hint: Remember to use 'is' for height and body shape, and 'has got' for hair, eyes, and face features. Speak slowly and clearly.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This storytelling task practises using 'be' and 'have got' together to give a complete physical description. Good descriptions include height, body type, hair, eyes, and special features.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell a short story about looking at a family photo. Describe two people in the photo. Use 'be' and 'have got' to describe their physical appearance.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: You are looking at a family photo. Choose two people in the photo and describe what they look like. Talk about their height, hair, eyes, and any special features.
storyPoints: Introduce the first person in the photo and describe their height, hair, and eyes.
Introduce the second person and describe how they look different from the first person.
Mention any accessories or special features for one or both people, such as glasses, a hat, or a moustache.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: In the photo, my grandmother is short. She has got long white hair and green eyes. My uncle is very tall. He has got short black hair and a big moustache. He wears sunglasses.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɪn ðə ˈfəʊtəʊ maɪ ˈɡrænmʌðər ɪz ʃɔːt. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ waɪt heər ænd ɡriːn aɪz. maɪ ˈʌŋkl ɪz ˈveri tɔːl. hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt blæk heər ænd ə bɪɡ məˈstɑːʃ. hiː weəz ˈsʌnɡlɑːsɪz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Describe two different people so you can practise contrasting descriptions. Use words like 'but' or 'and' to connect your sentences.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing two people in contrast helps you practise a wider range of appearance vocabulary. It also trains you to organise your ideas clearly when speaking.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are calling your friend to describe a person you saw at the park. Your friend wants to know what this person looks like. Describe the person's height, hair, and face.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ring ring! Your friend answers the phone and says: 'Hi! You said you saw someone interesting at the park. What does this person look like?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are on a phone call with your friend. You saw an interesting-looking person at the park today and you want to describe them. Your friend will ask you follow-up questions about the person's appearance.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student calling your friend to describe a stranger you saw at the park. Be descriptive and use 'be' and 'have got'.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: The person is very tall and thin. He has got long red hair and a beard. He has got a long face and big green eyes.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðə ˈpɜːsn ɪz ˈveri tɔːl ænd θɪn. hiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ red heər ænd ə bɪəd. hiː hæz ɡɒt ə lɒŋ feɪs ænd bɪɡ ɡriːn aɪz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with the person's height and body type, then move to hair and face details. Use 'has got' for features.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In this roleplay, you practise describing a person naturally in a phone conversation. This is a real-life situation where you need to paint a picture with words.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a lost-and-found office. A police officer asks you to describe your lost friend so they can help find them. Describe your friend's appearance clearly.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The police officer says: 'Hello. Can you describe your friend? What does your friend look like? Is your friend tall or short? What colour is their hair?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at a lost-and-found office in a shopping mall. You have lost your friend and a police officer needs a clear description to help find them. You must describe your friend's height, hair, eyes, and what makes them easy to recognise.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a worried student at a lost-and-found office. You need to describe your friend's physical appearance to a police officer so they can find your friend.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My friend is medium height and slim. She has got long straight black hair and dark brown eyes. She wears red glasses and she has got a round face.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ frend ɪz ˈmiːdiəm haɪt ænd slɪm. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ streɪt blæk heər ænd dɑːk braʊn aɪz. ʃiː weəz red ˈɡlɑːsɪz ænd ʃiː hæz ɡɒt ə raʊnd feɪs/
practicumQuestions.hint: Be very specific. The police officer needs details! Mention height, hair style, hair colour, eye colour, and special features like glasses.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing someone to help find them is a very practical real-life skill. You need to be clear and specific so the listener can identify the person.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are video-calling your pen pal for the first time. Your pen pal asks you to describe yourself. Tell them what you look like.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your pen pal says on the video call: 'Wow, it is so nice to finally see you! But my camera is not working well. Can you describe yourself for me? What do you look like?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are on a video call with your pen pal from another country. The video quality is very bad, so your pen pal asks you to describe your own physical appearance using words. This is the first time you are talking to each other.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student meeting your international pen pal on a video call for the first time. Describe your own appearance clearly and confidently.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I am quite short. I have got medium-length brown hair and dark eyes. I have got an oval face and I do not wear glasses.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ æm kwaɪt ʃɔːt. aɪ hæv ɡɒt ˈmiːdiəm leŋθ braʊn heər ænd dɑːk aɪz. aɪ hæv ɡɒt ən ˈəʊvl feɪs ænd aɪ duː nɒt weər ˈɡlɑːsɪz/
practicumQuestions.hint: You are describing yourself, so use 'I am' for height and 'I have got' for hair, eyes, and face. Be honest and detailed!
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describing yourself is one of the most common speaking tasks at A1 level. Using 'I am' and 'I have got' correctly shows good grammar control.

practicumQuestions.instruction: You are at a party and you see your teacher's new hairstyle. Your teacher asks you what you think. Describe what you notice about their new look.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Your teacher, Mrs. Sari, says: 'Hello! I have got a new hairstyle today. Can you describe how I look now? What is different about my hair?'
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are at a school party and your teacher, Mrs. Sari, has a new hairstyle. She used to have long straight hair, but now her hair is different. She asks you to describe her new appearance. Be polite and descriptive.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a polite student at a school party. You need to describe your teacher's new hairstyle and overall appearance. Use kind and descriptive words.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Mrs. Sari, you look very nice! You have got short curly hair now. It is brown with blonde highlights. Your hair looks really beautiful.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈmɪsɪz ˈsɑːri juː lʊk ˈveri naɪs. juː hæv ɡɒt ʃɔːt ˈkɜːli heər naʊ. ɪt ɪz braʊn wɪð blɒnd ˈhaɪlaɪts. jɔːr heər lʊks ˈrɪəli ˈbjuːtɪfl/
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with a compliment, then describe what you see. Use 'have got' to describe the new hair. Be polite!
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay practises describing changes in appearance and giving polite compliments. It combines appearance vocabulary with social language skills.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Focus on using the correct vocabulary words for physical appearance.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence clearly: 'My brother is medium height. He has got wavy blonde hair, blue eyes, and freckles.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: My brother is medium height. He has got wavy blonde hair, blue eyes, and freckles.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /maɪ ˈbrʌðər ɪz ˈmiːdiəm haɪt. hiː hæz ɡɒt ˈweɪvi blɒnd heər bluː aɪz ænd ˈfreklz/
practicumQuestions.hint: Focus on the appearance words: 'medium height', 'wavy', 'blonde', and 'freckles'. Make sure each word is clear and easy to understand.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill tests your knowledge of key appearance vocabulary. Words like 'wavy', 'blonde', and 'freckles' are essential for describing people at A1 level.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay attention to the correct use of 'be' for height and 'have got' for features.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Please say this sentence. Be careful with the grammar: 'She is short and slim. She has got long straight hair and she has not got a fringe.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: She is short and slim. She has got long straight hair and she has not got a fringe.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz ʃɔːt ænd slɪm. ʃiː hæz ɡɒt lɒŋ streɪt heər ænd ʃiː hæz nɒt ɡɒt ə frɪndʒ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'is' for body type (short, slim) and 'has got' for hair features. For the negative, say 'has not got'. Do not mix up 'is' and 'has got'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This grammar drill practises the two key structures for describing appearance: 'be + adjective' for height and body type, and 'have got + noun' for physical features. The negative form 'has not got' is also important.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following sentence out loud. Pay special attention to the syllable stress on the underlined words. Stress the capitalised syllables.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say this sentence and stress the correct syllables: 'She has got BEAU-ti-ful SHOUL-der-length hair and a mous-TACHE is not COM-mon for women.'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: She has got beautiful shoulder-length hair and a moustache is not common for women.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ʃiː hæz ɡɒt ˈbjuːtɪfl ˈʃəʊldə leŋθ heər ænd ə məˈstɑːʃ ɪz nɒt ˈkɒmən fɔːr ˈwɪmɪn/
practicumQuestions.hint: Stress the first syllable in BEAU-ti-ful, SHOUL-der, and COM-mon. Stress the second syllable in mous-TACHE. Say WI-men, not 'wo-men'.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Syllable stress changes the rhythm of English. Words like 'beautiful' (BEAU-ti-ful) and 'moustache' (mous-TACHE) have different stress positions. Practising these patterns helps you sound more natural.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the following two sentences out loud. Use FALLING intonation for the statement and RISING intonation for the yes/no question.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Say these two sentences with the correct intonation. First, the statement with falling intonation: 'He has got short grey hair.' Then, the question with rising intonation: 'Does he wear glasses?'
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: He has got short grey hair. Does he wear glasses?
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /hiː hæz ɡɒt ʃɔːt ɡreɪ heər ↘ dʌz hiː weər ˈɡlɑːsɪz ↗/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the statement 'He has got short grey hair', let your voice go DOWN at the end like going down a slide. For the question 'Does he wear glasses?', let your voice go UP at the end like climbing stairs.
practicumQuestions.explanation: In English, statements use falling intonation to show you are finished speaking. Yes/no questions use rising intonation to show you are asking and expecting an answer. This intonation pattern is very important for clear communication.
